corrections: 1) Claude desktop search is not an index. The transcript-search-worker scans on-disk JSONL transcripts per query with a case-insensitive substring match, capped at 200 recent sessions. It covers only local Claude Code Desktop (cowork/CCD) sessions, not claude.ai chats. So 'worker-backed index' should read 'worker-backed scan'. Hermes (FTS5 plus trigram, BM25) is the only verified indexed-search reference. 2) Prevalence: 'fork, versions and search are table-stakes (7-9 of 12)' overstates versions. Persisted regenerate/edit versions with a model or effort switch are 4 of 12 (C-t3-01-008), and the model/effort part is DOC-only (ChatGPT, Perplexity). The search counts also disagree across clusters: 7 of 12 in C-01-028, 3 of 12 in C-08-015 and 2 of 12 in C-13-015. Present search as table-stakes as a UI feature, but say that indexed full-text search plus an agent recall tool is verified only in Hermes (SRC), Claude CCD (a scan, SRC) and Cursor (SRC per records). 3) 'Hermes ... shows the mechanism' for versions is wrong. Hermes rewind is a confirmed truncation that archives the cut turns, with no sibling-version tree. The tree with 1/N versions comes from ChatGPT/Perplexity (DOC). Verevon's 'supersede, never delete' design is its own choice, closest to Hermes' archive-on-truncate. 4) The untrusted-snippet framing for the recall tool is verified in Claude (tool description) and DeepSeek (session-reference). It was not found as an explicit framing in Hermes session_search_tool.py.
caveats: Claude fork and search are local Claude Code Desktop session features (SRC), not claude.ai consumer chat. claude.ai chat search and branching are DOC.

corrections: 1) Codex is not a model for 'approve-then-continue'. Its Plan Mode tells the model not to ask whether to proceed; the user switches out of Plan mode and asks for implementation in a new turn, which is what Verevon does today. Keep Codex as best-in-class only for the decision-complete plan content. For a plan approval that resumes the same run, cite DeepSeek: its exit_plan_mode review is an ask_user wait with an Approve card, so approving resumes the run (SRC README). The C-t3-04-024 mechanism claim that the run 'then continues automatically' is not supported by the Codex evidence. 2) Manus is mis-attributed for questions. The SRC record (manus-product-ux-127) covers typed confirmation and approval socket messages (touchpoint, cascade workflow, connector re-OAuth, and similar), not clarifying questions. Manus structured questions with options are verified only through its public API docs (messageAskUser with question_expectation, DOC), and the answer goes back as a plain message. Either rephrase as 'Manus (DOC: question_expectation with single/multi options; SRC: typed confirmation messages for approvals)' or name Antigravity (SRC AskQuestion proto) or DeepSeek (SRC/DOC) as best for questions. 3) The 'rank' field in the ask_user schema comes only from Claude (drag-to-rank). Antigravity has options, multi-select, write-in and skip, but no rank.
caveats: Codex request_user_input is available only when listed for the turn (flag-gated); async variant per record, from binary strings only.
Cursor trays live in the workbench.glass bundle (new agent window); questions are gated by flags such as ask_question_all_modes per record.
DeepSeek timed questions are opt-in (shipped presets use blocking mode); the timed-card behaviour is documented in the package README plus an e2e test.
Claude ask_user_question is in the epitaxy (Claude Code desktop) surface and is SRC from analytics events, lazy-module ids and i18n strings, not traced logic.
Manus structured questions are DOC (public API); the Manus SRC evidence is approvals and confirmations only.
